findings.title: torch_compile=True aborts DP training on the first step for every supported dense HF causal-LM family: the now-default fused loss-only CE forward is not Dynamo-traceable under fullgraph=True
findings.claim: c0f95ced (#988) flipped `fused_linear_cross_entropy` from an explicit opt-in to `inherits from performance` (_factory.py:374-376, and DPTrainer always calls apply_model_patches(performance=True) at _dp_trainer.py:844-850), so the fused causal-LM forward wrapper is now installed on all 17 dense families in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`. The same commit made DPTrainer's *training* loss set the marker: `compute_per_example_loss` adds `loss_only=True` whenever `not return_logits and self._compute_loss_func is None and self._fused_forward_uses_marker` (_dp_trainer.py:2437-2442), which is exactly the training path. The wrapper's fused branch then executes `return_dict = return_dict if return_dict is not None else self.config.use_return_dict` (cross_entropy.py:257-259). In the pinned transformers 5.15.1, `PretrainedConfig.use_return_dict` is a deprecated property whose body is `logger.warning_once("`use_return_dict` is deprecated! ...")` (.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/configuration_utils.py:464-467). Meanwhile fae93a55 (#979) / afa0247f (#989) made the chunk compiler strict with no fallback: `_compile_strict_chunk` is `torch.compile(fn, backend=..., mode=..., fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` (_dp_trainer.py:209-218) and `_grad_compiler` wraps it with nothing else (_dp_trainer.py:4366-4369). Dynamo refuses to trace the logger call under fullgraph, the exception propagates through `_microbatch_accumulate_reduced` -> `training_step` -> `_synchronize_grad_failure` (which only special-cases torch.OutOfMemoryError, _dp_trainer.py:1310-1318) and the run dies. A second, independent blocker sits behind it: the portable chunked kernel's tile planner calls the pybind builtin `torch._C._functorch.is_gradtrackingtensor` (_linear_ce_chunked.py:96, reached from `_tile_plan` at :120), which Dynamo also cannot trace.
findings.failure_scenario: `DPTrainer(model=LlamaForCausalLM(...), args=TrainingArguments(torch_compile=True, ...)).train()` raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases` on step 1 and never trains. Reproduced on this tree (CPU, torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.15.1) for LlamaForCausalLM and Qwen2ForCausalLM. A/B isolation: the identical run with `performance_kernels_config={'fused_linear_cross_entropy': False}` compiles and completes its steps, and Phi3ForCausalLM (not in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`, so `_fused_forward_uses_marker` is False) also compiles and completes. Neutralizing only the deprecated property then exposes the second blocker: `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: Attempted to call function marked as skipped ... is_gradtrackingtensor`. `torch_compile` is documented as supported in docs/reference/transformers.md:218 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216. The existing compile tests cannot see this: packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_compile_and_kernel_args.py builds `nn.Linear` / a hand-written `_TinyLM` (lines 46, 56-67), neither of which receives the family patch, and the engine-level test packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping/test_compile_chunks.py compiles a pure tensor lambda.

findings.fix_sketch: In the fused wrapper, stop reading the deprecated property: transformers 5.x dropped `return_dict` from every causal-LM signature, so resolve it as `getattr(self.config, 'return_dict', True)` (or drop the tuple-return branch entirely and always build the ModelOutput). Then make `_vmap_batch_factor` Dynamo-safe (wrap the functorch probe in `torch._dynamo.disable`, or compute the tile plan outside the traced region and pass token/vocab tiles in as ints). Add a regression test that actually runs one compiled DP step on a registered HF family with the default patch set - that is the gap that let both blockers through. Separately, consider whether `_compile_strict_chunk` should fail loudly with a message naming the patch bucket rather than surfacing a raw Dynamo error mid-step.

findings.title: SFT loss-only DFT evaluation scores an unscaled-logit objective: `_fused_dft_loss_only` routes prediction_loss_only=True through `fused_dft_loss`, which ignores config logit scaling, so eval_loss measures a different objective than training on Cohere/Cohere2/Granite
findings.claim: 7edd41be (#929) added `self._fused_dft_loss_only = args.loss_type == 'dft' and self._lm_head_param_name is not None` (_sft_trainer.py:233-235) and widened the handle resolution to `_resolve_fused_handles(model, args.loss_type == 'dft')` (:230-232). The loss dispatch then became `elif self._fused_dft or (not return_logits and self._fused_dft_loss_only):` (:596), so a loss-only call takes the fused primitive even when `_fused_loss_eligible` is False. Because `SFTConfig.log_completion_metrics` defaults to True (_sft_config.py:90), `_fused_loss_eligible` and therefore `_fused_dft` are False at defaults - training keeps the eager `dft_loss(out.logits, labels)` path (:610-615) - while `prediction_step` asks for the no-logits closure whenever `prediction_loss_only` is set (:666-670), and `DPTrainer.evaluate()` sets `prediction_loss_only=True` whenever `compute_metrics is None` (_dp_trainer.py:3187). `fused_dft_loss` computes DFT against the raw projection `hidden @ lm_head_weight.T`: the fused branch calls `linear_nll_sum(...)` which hardcodes `logit_scale=1.0` (_fused_lce.py:113-114 and :120-122) and the eager fallback is `dft_loss(hidden_states @ lm_head_weight.transpose(-2,-1), labels)` (_dft.py:147). Neither applies `config.logit_scale` (Cohere/Cohere2, `logits = logits * self.logit_scale` in HF 5.15.1) nor `config.logits_scaling` (Granite, `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling`). This is the exact sibling the c0f95ced logit_scale work fixed for the model-level fused CE (cross_entropy.py:308-320, 336) and did not fix for the DFT primitive.
findings.failure_scenario: `SFTTrainer(model=CohereForCausalLM(...), args=SFTConfig(loss_type='dft', eval_strategy='steps', metric_for_best_model='eval_loss', load_best_model_at_end=True))`. Reproduced end to end on this tree: `trainer.evaluate()['eval_loss']` = 0.060834 while the training objective mean `dft_loss(model(...).logits, labels).mean()` = 0.064736 (6.0% off); Granite with logits_scaling=8.0 gives 0.063957 vs 0.064878 (1.4%). Per-batch: Cohere loss-only [0.059140, 0.062529] vs training/metrics-path [0.064630, 0.064842]; the metrics path (`prediction_loss_only=False`) matches training to 0.0, so the same checkpoint reports two different eval losses depending only on whether compute_metrics is configured - the exact inconsistency test_sft_dft_eval_loss_consistent_across_metric_modes was written to prevent, but that test only uses a tiny Llama (logit_scale absent) so it passes. Because the DFT weight is the detached softmax confidence, an unscaled temperature changes the per-token weighting, not just the value: with a synthetic logit_scale of 8 the gap is 633x. Sibling path (untouched by this commit, same root cause): with `log_completion_metrics=False` the same `fused_dft_loss` becomes the *training* objective (`_fused_dft` True), so a DP-SFT run on Cohere/Granite optimizes a differently-tempered DFT loss than the one documented in _dft.py, silently.

findings.fix_sketch: Thread the family scale into the DFT primitive the same way c0f95ced did for the model-level fused CE: give `linear_nll_sum` a `logit_scale` parameter (it already forwards positionally into kernels that accept one) and give `fused_dft_loss` a `logit_scale` / `logit_softcapping` argument, applied in both the fused and the eager `hidden @ W.T` fallback. `SFTTrainer.compute_per_example_loss` (:596-605) should read `config.logit_scale` / `config.logits_scaling` / `config.final_logit_softcapping` off `self._model.config` and pass them. findings.title: The fused-CE wrapper's non-fused fallback branch recomputes logits without family logit scaling, silently changing the trained objective and the returned logits on the CUDA fp32 path
findings.claim: When a loss-only call is made but the fused kernel is declined, the wrapper falls through to `logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :]); loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs)` (cross_entropy.py:358-364). That branch reproduces stock Llama's tail and nothing else: it does not apply `config.logit_scale` (Cohere/Cohere2), `config.logits_scaling` (Granite) or `config.final_logit_softcapping`, all of which the wrapper *does* compute and pass into the kernels on the fused branch (:308-320, :336). The declining condition is `use_fused_ce = loss_only and _supported and ((hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype in (bf16, fp16)) or not hidden_states.is_cuda)` (:282-289): on CUDA with fp32 hidden states the whole expression is False, so the fallback runs. c0f95ced made this reachable for the plain DPTrainer at defaults, because it both installs the wrapper unconditionally (_factory.py:374-376) and makes the DP training loss set `loss_only=True` (_dp_trainer.py:2437-2442). Before that commit the wrapper was opt-in and DPTrainer never sent a marker, so only an explicit `fused_linear_cross_entropy=True` (or SFT chunked_nll) could reach this branch.
findings.failure_scenario: DP fine-tuning a Cohere/Cohere2/Granite checkpoint on CUDA where the backbone's last hidden state is fp32 (i.e. the model was not loaded in half precision; note bf16 autocast does not necessarily make it bf16, because RMSNorm multiplies by an fp32 weight before returning). Every training step then computes the per-example loss - and its gradient - from unscaled logits, and `output.logits` handed back to eval / compute_metrics is likewise unscaled. Nothing warns. Forced-branch measurement on this tree (entered via the `weight` kwarg, which trips the same `_fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported` decline at :286-287): Cohere native loss 4.853949 vs fallback 4.898671, max |logit| difference 1.189; Granite (logits_scaling=8.0) 4.853372 vs 4.873374, max |logit| difference 0.563; Llama 0.0 difference. I could not execute the CUDA+fp32 gate in this CPU-only sandbox - that half of the reachability chain is read from :282-289 - but the branch's arithmetic defect is demonstrated directly.

findings.fix_sketch: Hoist the family-scaling resolution (`logit_scale`, `logits_scaling`, `final_logit_softcapping`) above the `if use_fused_ce:` branch and apply it to `logits` in the fallback before calling `self.loss_function` - `logits = logits * logit_scale` and, when softcap is set, `softcap * tanh(logits / softcap)` - so both branches produce the model-native logits. Better still, make the fallback delegate to `original(...)` (it already has every argument it needs) instead of re-implementing the tail, which removes this whole class of drift. Extend test_fused_ce_text_family_parity to cover cohere/granite/gemma2 on BOTH branches (fused and declined).

clean_areas: Dynamic-shape graph reuse, numerics: ran the strict chunk compiler (`_compile_strict_chunk`, fullgraph=True + dynamic=True) against an eager `clipped_grad` over 11 realized batch sizes {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,13} with microbatch_size=4 (so full, remainder and size-1 chunks all occur). Summed clipped gradients, per-example grad_norms, clipping_rate and batch_size were bit-identical to eager with backend=aot_eager (max diff 0.0), and within fp32 reassociation noise (<=1.9e-06) with backend=inductor on CPU including second_moment=True. No evidence that a graph compiled for one chunk size is reused for another in a way that changes numerics, and no silent padding of the leading dimension.

Dynamic-shape graph reuse, adaptive and per-group clipping: repeated the same differential test for `adaptive_clipped_grad` (runtime threshold crossing the compiled boundary as a tensor, 7 steps incl. an empty draw) and for `PerGroup` clipping (2 groups, 5 batch sizes incl. 0 and 1). Compiled and eager agreed exactly on gradients, `max_norm`, the adapted `_next_clipping_norm` sequence, and the per-group `group_norms` shapes. `_tensor_clipping_norm` (_clipped_fun.py:202-224) does keep the threshold out of the guard set, so a changing adaptive norm does not force recompiles or value specialization.

Empty-batch path (#808 / OPQ-334) regression check: `clipped_grad`, `auto_clipped_grad` and `adaptive_clipped_grad` all still short-circuit on batch_size==0 before any vmap or compiled kernel (_clipped_grad.py:322,337,348; _adaptive.py:452). Verified that the empty response matches the non-empty step's pytree structure, key names after a structure-changing `pre_clipping_transform`, leaf dtype under `dtype=torch.float32` with bf16 params, `max_norm`, and the paired second-moment shape - all four factories agreed. The compiled chunk kernel never observes a zero-length chunk because `range(0, batch_size, microbatch_size)` cannot emit one for batch_size>0, and the empty batch bypasses the kernel entirely.

Eval accumulator ordering and padding (1633673e): unit-tested `_PredictionAccumulator` over 24 combinations of eval_accumulation_steps in {1,2,3,None} x 1..9 batches with varying per-batch sizes (1-3) and varying sequence lengths (2-5). Verified that the balanced binary chunk tree in `_append_cold_chunk` plus the `_ordered_cold_chunks` reversal restores strict oldest-to-newest row order for predictions, labels, inputs and losses simultaneously, and that short sequences are padded with -100 only in the trailing positions (losses, being 1-D, are never padded). No cross-container misalignment between `losses` and `label_ids`.

Eval transfer overlap, memory safety: read `_CpuTransferPipeline` / `_stage_cuda_nested` for read-before-write and use-after-free. The side stream waits on the producer (`self._stream.wait_stream(producer)`), the CUDA source is kept alive for the copy via `value.record_stream(stream)`, the pinned destination is retained in `_PendingCpuTransfer.payload` until `completed.synchronize()`, and `_to_pageable_nested` only releases pinned memory after that sync. The queue is FIFO with `max_pending=2` and `_drain_one` is called before enqueueing a new transfer, so cold chunks are consumed in submission order. The one ordering hazard in the code - `submit`'s early return for an all-CPU payload (_eval.py:241-250) bypasses the pending queue - is not reachable in practice, because `_first_cuda_device` scans the whole payload and on a CUDA run at least one of losses/logits/labels/inputs is always device-resident.

Eval telemetry: `_EvaluationTelemetry.finish()` is idempotent, synchronizes before reading CUDA events, and `_interval_overlap` is a standard two-pointer sweep over chronologically ordered intervals; division guards exist for zero transfer time and `StepPerf` guards zero elapsed time, so an empty or streaming eval set cannot divide by zero.

OPQ-325 base-trainer fix (25bb4ed7): confirmed `prediction_step`'s batched branch now calls `self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` (_dp_trainer.py:2714-2721) and rebuilds label-smoothed CE from logits when a custom loss is absent (:2726-2758), and that the `loss_only` marker is suppressed whenever `_compute_loss_func is not None` (:2700-2706), so the fused logits-free path cannot swallow a custom objective. The SFT override delegates to this path for every loss_type except dft.

Fused loss-only CE numerical parity on the fused branch: compared the wrapper's `loss_only=True` loss against the stock HF loss on CPU for llama, cohere, cohere2, granite (logits_scaling 0.5/1.0/8.0), gemma, gemma2 (softcap 5.0/30.0) and exaone4 - relative error <= 2e-07 in every case, and `logits` is None as contracted. The `logit_scale` refactor in c0f95ced (weight-copy -> per-tile scalar, with the matching chain rule at linear_cross_entropy.py:412-414 and _linear_ce_chunked.py:386) is numerically correct on this branch; the chunked kernel's label-smoothing formula `(1-eps)*nll + eps*(lse - sum_logits/V)` also matches `F.cross_entropy(label_smoothing=eps)` and the smoothed `sum_logits` is accumulated from the scaled tile.

Fused-CE install gate: `_fused_linear_ce_supports_class`'s escape clause `or not target_cls.__module__.startswith('transformers.models.')` is currently inert - every registered family in packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/*.py points at a `transformers.models.*` module path - so no unregistered/custom causal-LM class silently receives the generic fused forward. Verified that `_fused_forward_uses_marker` stays False for families outside `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM` (checked live with Phi3ForCausalLM), so the marker is never sent to a forward that cannot accept it.

Loss-only DFT closure caching (7edd41be): `_get_eval_per_example_loss_fn` keeps two independent caches keyed on `self._model` identity (`_eval_per_example_loss_fn` vs `_eval_per_example_loss_only_fn`), so the logits and no-logits vmap closures cannot be swapped for one another, and `prediction_step` unpacks `output` as a scalar only on the `prediction_loss_only` branch. No shape or arity confusion between the two closures.

DDP/empty-batch interaction with strict compilation: `training_step` routes any rank-local grad failure - explicitly including a first-call compilation failure on a non-empty rank while a sibling skipped the kernel on an empty Poisson draw - through `_synchronize_grad_failure` before the gradient AllReduce (_dp_trainer.py:2198-2212), so a compile error is rank-symmetric rather than a hang. `_sync_clipping_rate` issues the same two collectives on empty and non-empty ranks (engine/clipping/_distributed.py:222-247).
